M-VAVE

Official Open

Latest V14 Updated 19 Oct 2026 313313 stars on GitHub

M-VAVE's own open-source firmware, which turns the FM1 into an eight-track groovebox: each track plays a DX7, 303, 808, PSG, Pluck, or sampler engine, with 16 USER project slots and an eight-slot sample bank every project shares. It installs from M-VAVE's FM1 Workbench, which also edits projects, simulates the device, and can put V15 back. This editor recognises it and sends it no Program Change or effect controls, which would change its tracks, but sends it no patches yet: a DX7 track takes a voice or bank downloaded from this editor as a .syx file, through the Workbench.

V14 holds 128 independent DX7 voices in four groups of 32 and takes DX7 single-voice and 32-voice bank SysEx.

Going back: the Workbench's Restore original V15 replaces all four banks with the factory voices, and a force flash may erase projects and samples, so download a backup from this editor first.

M-VAVE

Stock firmware

Works with this editor Latest V16 Updated 21 Oct 2026 Not on GitHub

The firmware every FM1 ships with: a six-operator FM engine compatible with DX7 voices, four banks of 32 presets, effects, an arpeggiator, and a sequencer. Install it with M-VAVE's M-UPGRADE tool, which is also the way back from Felucca and SLOOP. V16, released on 21 October, makes the FM1 eight-part multitimbral, with 20 voices shared between the parts, longer patterns, and one library of 128 effect settings that every preset shares; this editor has not been tested with it yet.

Going back: download the stock firmware from M-VAVE's downloads, under PC Firmware, and install it over whichever firmware the FM1 runs; many custom firmwares' own installers can put it back too. If SLOOP, or a firmware built on it such as sloopDX or zp12, no longer starts, hold OCT− alone while switching the FM1 on: it starts in USB rescue, ready to install again.

M-VAVE also publishes a groovebox firmware of its own, Official Open, listed above.

Baud Girl

Baud Girl (FM-1+VA)

Works with this editor Latest FM-1_102 Updated 19 Oct 2026 Not on GitHub

Keeps M-VAVE's FM engine and effects, fixes its engine bugs, and adds a Virtual Analog engine, an 8-Bit engine, a Bitcrush effect, a 64-step sequencer, and a Note Engine for arpeggios, auto-arpeggios, and auto-chords. It installs from Baud Girl's own browser page, keeps your presets, and can put M-VAVE's firmware back. This editor reads and writes its FM, Virtual Analog, and 8-Bit presets, effects included, keeps the 8-Bit ones in the library, and downloads them as presets files.

FM-1 firmware patcher

Works with this editorPatches V15 and V16 Updated 28 Oct 2026 1111 stars on GitHub

A script that changes your own copy of M-VAVE's V15 or V16 rather than a firmware of its own: operator detune matches Dexed, aftertouch no longer brings a strong vibrato, and the main screen's scope turns dark blue. The FM1 still reports V15 or V16, so this editor treats it as M-VAVE's firmware.

The patched file may not be shared, so you run the Python script yourself. M-UPGRADE sees it as the V15 already installed, so go down to V14 with M-VAVE's tone updater first, then install it; the same steps put V15 back.

smememe

FM-1 Macropad Patch

Works with this editorPatches V15 · Latest 1.0.0 Updated 12 Oct 2026 33 stars on GitHub

A patcher, not a firmware, which changes your own copy of M-VAVE’s V15 so that every button, key, and knob sends a USB-MIDI note, fourteen buttons, 27 keys, and seven knobs each way, which an app such as Keyboard Maestro or MidiKey2Key turns into shortcuts. The synth functions go, and so does the settings screen, so set the velocity you want with M-VAVE’s firmware before patching.

The patched file may not be shared, so you download V15 yourself and patch it in the web page or with Python, then install it with M-UPGRADE. Its README says no recovery method is known if an update fails; M-VAVE’s updater puts V15 back.

MidiHax

FM-1 MIDI Processor

Latest 0.1.0 Updated 3 Nov 2026 00 stars on GitHub

A stand-alone MIDI processor, with no computer needed. The synth is removed, so the only sound is a metronome click. MIDI from TRS and USB goes through a pipeline and comes out of USB, with a searchable monitor showing what it did to each message, per-port channel and message filters, and message and channel remaps. Event triggers send a list of messages, such as the bank and program changes for a whole rig, from one incoming message. The knobs send CCs, the keys play notes and send program and bank changes, and clock lockout keeps clocks from being merged. It holds 16 named patches, which can be dumped and loaded over SysEx, and it is built on the Official Open V14 source. Latency measured on an FM-1 averages under 0.2 ms. It installs from its own page in desktop Chrome or Edge over USB.

Watch list

Firmwares on their way that cannot be installed on an FM1 yet. Each joins the list above once it can.

  • Blop ↗ OSR-Experiment

    A chord-grid firmware by Obsimo, with one-finger chords, chord rhythms, a kick with sidechain, glide, and reverb, with its notes in French. Its release holds a firmware package, but its README calls it a prototype that has never been tested on an FM1.

  • FM-1 Piano ↗ FartyPants

    A hybrid physically modelled piano squeezed into 500 kB. It has a nightly browser installer and emulator, but no release and no licence file, and its README calls it a work in progress.

  • DEEP FIELD ↗ WisestWizard

    An ambient drone machine on fm1-base, in a repository shared with the Pocket Poly polysynth. Its README calls the tree a scaffold in development, and there is no release or installer.

  • AEther ↗ twaroshinto

    A spectral synthesiser inspired by Paul's Extreme Sound Stretch, with its notes in Polish. Its README says 0.5 has not been tested on an FM1, and there is no release yet.

  • AMARU OS ↗ MarcoCasanova00

    A firmware fusing Bunker Evolved, JIANT's tekno, and the character of Carnac OS and Mycelium. Its README calls it an alpha that has never been flashed on an FM1, and there is no release yet.

  • AMBII ↗ MilkBoyG

    An ambient firmware built on Melodee, for slow, expressive sound design and performance. So far it is a browser prototype, with no FM1 build released.

  • Argo ↗ echoe

    A Felucca fork whose description says it has many changes to run via a local LLM. Its repository has no README, release, or installer yet.

  • Atmosphere OS ↗ codemtm

    An ambient and dub techno firmware. It is built from source only: the v1.0 release has no installable package, and the status file says it has not yet had a device build or hardware test.

  • Betis Mode ↗ cotrino

    A Real Betis-themed firmware built on M-VAVE's FM1 Open SDK, with a browser emulator and a downloadable package. Its README says no FM1 has been flashed with it yet.

  • Bliss Box ↗ manzanita-research

    A new-age ambient firmware, built from source with no release or installer. Its README says it is a prototype that has not been on an FM1 yet.

  • BlueHare ↗ tristanosuriani

    A Felucca-based firmware with a tracker interface. It is built from source, with no release, package or installer of its own, and its README is still Felucca's.

  • BREAK//174 ↗ EremanSim

    A jungle instrument: PLAY starts a groove at 166 BPM to cut up with rolls, reverse, and dub throws. Its alpha package is in the repository, but its README, in Russian, says it has not yet been tried on an FM1.

  • Cat Piano ↗ thefriendlyhedgehog

    A piano of real meows in four banks, with a sequencer and an arpeggiator. Its README says it runs on an FM1, but it is built from source, with no release or installer.

  • COSMOS ↗ gadlele

    A drone synth firmware still at the design stage. Only a COSMOS PROBE test firmware can be installed (a browser page that tests WiFi and memory); the instrument itself has no release.

  • CRATE ↗ zisonzishen

    A slice and performance sampler that takes samples over USB. It is published as source, with no release or installer.

  • Deal or No Deal ↗ Kiwi3p

    A parody of the game show. It is built from source as a preview, with no release or installer.

  • drift-fm1 ↗ I-am-MaxPower

    An Omnichord-style drone firmware. It has no release or installer page of its own: its README explains how to build one from a fork.

  • duodrone ↗ pjac1810

    A drone firmware on foma, by SPELLBOX’s maker. Its README, in French, explains how to build it, but there is no release or installer page yet.

  • Erik37 ↗ genkigenki

    A sampled concert grand written for the SMK-37. Its page offers an FM1 build of 1.2, which its README says is untested on a unit.

  • FM Stud1o ↗ MPASTEAU

    An eight-track groovebox on Felucca 1.6.1, with a piano roll, a drum grid, a song mode, and a mixer. It is built from source, with no release or installer.

  • FM-1 Felucca-Tutor ↗ wochende

    An interactive tutorial on Felucca that teaches synthesis, sequencing, and song building on the FM1's screen. It is published as source, with no release, installer, or licence.

  • fm-dub ↗ imijes

    A dub-flavoured fork of SLOOP. It has no releases, and its README and package are unchanged SLOOP 2.5, so nothing installable of its own is offered; install SLOOP itself instead.

  • fm1-1971 ↗ synthi

    A generative ambient fork of Melodee 1.3.5. It has no release of its own, and its README still points to Melodee’s installer.

  • fm1-amy ↗ dpwe

    AMY's emulations of the Roland Juno-60's 128 factory patches as a six-voice synth, built on X0X. Its README says it has been installed and played on one FM1, but it offers no release or package: it is built from source.

  • fm1-beets ↗ mattb

    Beets as firmware, with a browser version and a TouchOSC visualiser. It is built from source, with no release or installer.

  • fm1-ctrl ↗ johnskiller

    A thin firmware, by DriftSeq’s maker, that makes the FM1 a hardware controller for web emulators. It has no release or build to install yet.

  • fm1-insert-coin ↗ DarkHelmet67

    1980s arcade games for the FM1, starting with Space Invaders. Its README, in Italian, says the first game is still being written, and builds come only from its CI runs until it is finished.

  • fm-1-monomachine ↗ sirpearson

    A firmware after Elektron’s Monomachine. Its README, in Italian, calls it experimental and says it has not yet run on real hardware.

  • fm1-p6 ↗ Jonbenderr

    A Polysix emulation, published only as a source archive.

  • fm1-sampler ↗ ferluht

    An eight-track sampler and audio looper whose sound comes from an Android app, with the FM1 as its keys, knobs, screen, and USB audio output. Its README says it has been tested only on a computer, not on a phone or an FM1.

  • FM-1 Studio Tess ↗ jamesusmusic

    A fork of Melodee (Tess). Its package is kept in the repository with install instructions, but there is no release or installer page, and its README says full hardware testing is still to come.

  • fm1-t1 ↗ tensor-programming

    A firmware with Torso T1 functionality. Its README calls it a work in progress, with no release or installer.

  • FM-Tracker ↗ drok123

    A tracker firmware based on SLOOP. Its README calls it a research and host-side prototype, with no flashable firmware yet.

  • fm1-wave ↗ johnskiller

    A polyphonic wavetable synth on fm1-base, by DriftSeq’s maker. So far its README is fm1-base’s template, and there is no release.

  • fm1wheel ↗ ograndebe

    A tonewheel organ firmware after setBfree, built on fm1-base. Its README says only its first phase is complete, on a computer, and there is no release yet.

  • FM2K ↗ jukejutsu

    A song-maker firmware prototype. It runs in a simulator only, with no release or installer, and the README says not to install it on an FM-1 yet.

  • FNTSMG-1 ↗ fantasmogenesis

    A groovebox firmware on Felucca, with eight tracks, eighteen engines of its own, and eight-track USB audio; its notes are in Spanish. It has no GitHub release, and its web installer is a closed beta of 30 places, by registration, ahead of a public launch set for 16 Nov 2026.

  • FOUROBOROS ↗ Ignignot

    A firmware built on SLOOP and Felucca. Its repository holds only an installer page for a V1 smoke candidate, whose hardware verification is pending, and nothing that says what it does.

  • genAMB ↗ Kayman18

    A generative firmware based on AMB-1, with two pad synths, a Rings port, a six-voice FM synth, and sequencers ported from VCV Rack. Its 1.0 RC2 package is in the repository, but its notes say it has not been booted on an FM1, and no licence is stated.

  • Glitchbox ↗ erikdevos

    Its README calls it experimental and says it has run only in host tests and the browser emulator, not yet on an FM1.

  • GRIDLIGHT ↗ pjac1810

    A 16 × 16 light-grid sequencer after Yamaha's Tenori-On, by SPELLBOX's maker. Its README, in French, mentions a web installer, but there is no release yet.

  • Haave ↗ thebrodi

    A simple, dreamy ambient firmware for live meditation, a Felucca fork, formerly called Drift. Its README says it runs on its maker's FM1 and in a browser emulator, but there is no public release to install yet.

  • DriftSeq ↗ johnskiller

    A 16-track polymetric sequencer. Its web emulator is live, but there is no firmware build yet.

  • FM-PLAITS ↗netroxic

    A generative Plaits voice built on M-VAVE's FM1 Open V14. It has a web installer page and a browser version, but no release and no licence file, and nothing says it has run on an FM1.

  • fm1-doom ↗ Keitark

    Doom's engine on the FM1, by FM-1 NES's author. Its firmware and the loading of game data are still being written, and no build is offered for installing.

  • FM1 MDX karaoke player ↗ Keitark

    Plays MDX and PDX songs on a software YM2151 and lets you mute a part and play it on the keys. It has been tested on a computer but not yet installed on an FM1.

  • FM1 Move ↗ Nicodesy06

    An eight-track groovebox built from SLOOP. Its device page can install it, and community testers have run earlier builds on FM1s, but there has been no structured hardware test.

  • fm1-polyseq ↗ NOVALENTI

    A polyphonic 16-step sequencer and hardware layer written from scratch in C. It is published as source only.

  • fm1-zed ↗ cmlarsen

    A custom firmware based on Felucca. It has no release of its own yet.

  • FM80S ↗ y6zkcqnf5r-hue

    A synth-looper: play a loop on the keys, then another instrument over it, or program one step by step. It is being written in a browser first, and its notes are in French.

  • IVee ↗ awolace

    A generative firmware with shared harmony, evolving patterns, and live keys. So far its repository holds only a README.

  • K-GLITCH ↗ Guizmoh

    A glitch machine and chaos generator built from KAWA, by its maker. Its README says its newest feature has not yet been compiled for the FM1, and there is no release.

  • KAWA ↗ Guizmoh

    A tracker with a web installer, a manual, and a sample importer. Its README calls 0.6 a beta that has not yet been tried on an FM1.

  • LSDJ Burrito ↗ dreamsofbacon

    A GameDude fork for running your own copy of LSDj, formerly called LSDj for FM-1. Its page has switched installing off, since an earlier version of the installer left an FM1 unable to start, and for now only checks that your ROM is a version tested on the FM1.

  • Lunar Modulator ↗ ip2k

    Open firmware with engines derived from Mutable Instruments' modules and a Movy-style sequencer. It runs only as a virtual FM1 in a browser, and has never written anything to an FM1.

  • Maestro ↗ node56

    Music lessons on the FM1’s screen, with note-reading, rhythm, and sight-reading drills graded on pitch and timing. Its README calls it a scaffold, with the on-device screen and sound still to be connected.

  • MD-One ↗ d0pe1

    A drone machine built from Mutable Instruments' engines. Its README says it was first flashed to its maker's FM1 on 22 Oct, but there is no release or installer yet.

  • more chords ↗ rosen-wav

    A ChoralRoot remix with engines adapted from Melodee and ORBIT. It has a web installer page and an emulator, but no release and no licence stated.

  • Mutable Dreams 1.1 Ghoul ↗ alexwlloyd

    An editor and installer site for a Ghoul build of Mutable Dreams 1.1. Its package is in the repository, but the site is not published, it is not verified on an FM1, and no licence is stated.

  • mvave-fm1-mpe ↗ monch1962

    A Felucca fork that plays MPE. It is built from source, with no release or installer of its own.

  • My Name is Mod ↗ yentzee

    A generative firmware based on Felucca, with 64 steps and four patterns. So far its repository holds only a licence.

  • NESynth ↗ ChanceTheMaker

    An NES emulator, by GameDude’s maker. Its FM1 build is still on a feature branch, and its releases so far are for the SMK-37.

  • NoteSorcery ↗ catacombius

    An eight-track firmware that works with Ableton and an Android app. BOTANICA, a firmware built on it with felt piano and droplet engines, has pre-releases, the latest 0.3, each with a firmware package and a web installer. Its release notes say it has been tested only in a simulator and by CI, not yet on an FM1.

  • NSX39 Pocket Miku ↗ AL-255

    A vocal firmware for the Gakken NSX39 Pocket Miku. Its release is source and a browser generator, which builds the package from your own dump of an NSX39's flash chip, so there is no ready package to install.

  • OCTODRONE ↗ pjac1810

    An eight-voice drone synth after the SOMA Laboratory Lyra-8, by SPELLBOX's maker. Its README, in French, mentions a web installer, but there is no release yet.

  • ODeath WAVE-1 ↗gybe808-dotcom

    A Felucca mod with a wavetable synth of 20 waveforms and nine presets. It has an installer page with its firmware bundled, but no release and no licence file, and nothing says it has run on an FM1.

  • Oktowave ↗ PierreArnaudGUYOT

    Felucca 1.6.1 with a WAVELET engine from the Wavelet Synthesizer, and 108 of its presets. Its README says version 0.1 has not been run on an FM1 yet.

  • Opslix ↗ FroggyDenim

    A firmware after the Korg Opsix. Its repository has no README, release, or installer yet.

  • OrganVave-1 ↗ ruppert

    A Hammond B3 and Leslie emulation. Its README says nothing in it has been tested on a real FM1 yet, and there is no release.

  • Patricktronics ↗ gaumondp

    A generative layer on Felucca. It has install instructions but no release, and has not been confirmed on an FM1.

  • Pelucco ↗ Gadlele

    A Felucca fork by Golana’s maker. It has no release of its own, and its README is still Felucca’s.

  • Pin Head ↗ TruBitTech

    A pin-matrix firmware after the EMS Synthi AKS. Its repository holds a demo page and the start of its source, with no release or licence.

  • REGGAE-OS ↗ KemstheSage

    A reggae synth firmware based on Felucca. Its notes call it an early development build whose hardware is untested.

  • Rhizome ↗ Dr-John-8bits

    An ambient firmware derived from Monades, with an orbital sequencer, granular synthesis, a hall reverb, and a tape delay. Its README, in French, says it has not yet been compiled or measured on an FM1 and asks you not to install it.

  • RIFT ↗ Vaayaa

    Its README, in Chinese, explains how to build and install it, but there is no release or installer page.

  • RIFT by mykeln ↗ mykeln

    An experimental drone instrument derived from Felucca, with nine modes and stereo feedback. Its README says 0.1 booted on an FM1 and 0.2 awaits hardware confirmation, with no release or installer yet. It is not Vaayaa's RIFT.

  • Rocket OS ↗ cmlarsen

    A clip-launching performance firmware forked from X0X. It has no build of its own yet.

  • SLICE64-FM ↗ jeymadcat-ops

    A four-track tracker with SID, FM, and sampler engines. Its web editor is public, but the firmware is not yet.

  • TamaMPE ↗ tamabotmusic

    An MPE synth firmware based on Melodee. It has no release or installer of its own, only an emulator page and the source.

  • TripDeck ↗ anonymousacademe

    A psychedelic synth whose every screen is an animated picture. Its README says 0.2 runs on the FM1, but it is built from source, with no release or installer.

  • Type P ↗ CeliaCasanovas

    A two-part, four-operator phase distortion synth, written with its maker’s own umetate framework as a test of it. It has no release yet.

  • UNIBOX ↗ chinotto1

    A nine-track groovebox built on FOMAJAM, with an arranger, free recording, and a USB sampler. It is published as source only.

  • URANUS 88 ↗ hagan66

    An eight-voice analogue-style polysynth on fm1-dock, with its notes in Swedish. Its package comes only from its CI runs, with no release yet, and there is no licence file.

  • Vector37 ↗ genkigenki

    An orbiting overtone synth written for the SMK-37 keyboard. Its page lists a 0.3.2 build for the FM1, and its README says it has not been tried on one.

  • Velo ↗ charlesvestal

    Velocity and aftertouch from the FM1’s keys, with no hardware changes. Its README says it works but is parked with its calibration unfinished, and it is built from source.

  • VNL-1 ↗ pianomansam

    A lo-fi hip hop firmware on fm1-base. It is built from source, with no release or installer.

  • Wild ↗ saintpid

    An experimental n001se fork. It is built from source, with no release, package or installer, and the README says it is untested on hardware.

  • WitchBox ↗ davidpryan

    A six-track 2-step and melodic dubstep groovebox on Dinghy. Its README says it builds and renders audio on a computer but has not yet run on an FM1.

  • WT-2 ↗ DedrichVonDorn

    A wavetable synth with 206 parameters, installed through M-VAVE's M-UPGRADE app. Its README says to take the package from the Releases page once it is published, and there is no release yet.

  • Zombie FM-1 ↗ Joolo09

    Two firmwares, a groovebox and a sampler, with DAW modes for FL Studio and Ableton Live and a web installer. Its README says flashing a physical FM1 has not been verified.

  • VirtuoX ↗ telespial

    Piano learning and DX7-style synthesis. So far it is a browser prototype: its README says no flashable firmware has been released.

  • MODFM1 ↗ JoshCowley

    A sound-design rack of Mutable Instruments modules that plays in a browser. Its repository holds two installable packages, but its README says nothing has run on an FM1 yet.

  • PHREAK ↗ dagnazty

    A six-track groovebox on SLOOP 2.8.4, with three synth tracks and three drum tracks whose kits come from a USB stick. Its README says 1.2 has been tested on one FM1, but there is no release: you build the package yourself or serve its installer from your own computer.

Pictures come from each project's own pages. Know of a firmware missing here? Open an issue.
